title: Two officers' 'lives at risk' when they killed man
article: Two police officers were in a "life-and-death" situation, and needed to fire all 15 pistol rounds they discharged at Gerald Samuel Chenery, who was attacking them with serrated steak knives on Boxing Day, Vancouver police said Wednesday.
Chenery was hit by 12 of the 15 bullets and died of his wounds.

"None of us come to work wanting to shoot somebody," department spokesman Const. Howard Chow said in releasing a preliminary report on Chenery's death. "But sometimes we are faced with life-and-death situations, much as these two officers were faced with that night."
Chow said the officers fired their weapons 15 times because the bullets were not stopping Chenery from swinging the two steak knives at the officers.
"It was only this 15th round that caused Mr. Chenery to stop," Chow said, adding the entire exchange took place over a very short period of time.
He said Chenery was carrying four steak knives, and was wanted on a Canada-wide warrant because his parole had been revoked.
Chenery had been released from prison three days earlier, Chow said, after serving 18 months for robbery.
Chow said he did not know the reason Chenery's parole had been revoked, but said it is not unheard of for someone to have a warrant out for their arrest so soon after being released from prison.
Chow said the two officers encountered Chenery while conducting a routine patrol in their cruiser along Hastings Street on Boxing Day.
Chow said a man, later identified as Chenery, began walking away as soon as he saw the police officers, which caused them to stop their car and investigate.
When the officers, a man and a woman, asked the suspect if he was armed, Chenery, whom Chow described as "considerably larger" than the female officer, pulled a serrated steak knife.
Chow said the two officers made "loud and clear demands" for Chenery to drop the knife, but he failed to do so.
Instead, he said, Chenery pulled a second knife and charged at the female officer.
In response she fired four shots at Chenery, only one of which hit him, Chow said.
Unhindered by the bullet, Chenery began slashing at the female officer with both knives, Chow said.
It was at that point, Chow said, that the male officer fired 10 shots at Chenery from his semi-automatic Beretta pistol. All the shots hit him, either in his back, wrists or leg.
Chenery then started moving toward the male officer, Chow said, at which point the male officer fired the final, and fatal, shot.
Chenery was taken to St. Paul's Hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Doctors found two shots had inflicted serious lung damage, and one had nicked his heart.
The investigation is continuing, Chow said, adding that the results will be handed to the police complaints commission and the coroner.
The two officers, whom he did not identify, are back on active duty, he added.

Chow said the fact that the two officers each had less than a year's experience had nothing to do with the shooting, and that when their lives are in danger all officers are trained to fire their weapons until the threat ends.
Chow extended the department's sympathies to the family of Chenery. They could not be reached Wednesday to comment.
